title: The Wild Ember
premise: Isandro Okafor, the last swordspeaker sworn to the Ledger Guild, has spent years hiding among impossible trades—bottled storms, borrowed memories, second chances. When a century-old prophecy book names tonight's date and her own true name, she learns the guild's founding covenant between the human realms and the dying dragons was broken by her predecessors, and that every 'impossible thing' they trade is stolen dragon-fire. Hunted by her own guild and courted by a fugitive dragon-warden named Sefu, Isandro must gather the scattered oath-stones of the original swordspeakers and reforge the covenant at the Emberhold before the last dragon's flame gutters out. In the end she chooses justice over law: she burns the ledgers, returns what was stolen, and binds herself not to a guild but to a found family of outcasts who carry the renewed covenant together.
about_author: Jonah Ishikawa is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing rare manuscripts before turning to fantasy full-time. They write stories about people who keep promises in worlds that have forgotten how.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. A night of routine trades at the guildhouse: a bottled storm sold, a memory pawned. Isandro balances the ledgers with quiet pride, keeping herself invisible as always. Emotional beat: competent solitude, the comfort of rules—until the final entry refuses to be written.

chapters.title: Tonight, By Name
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. An old client trades a water-damaged prophecy book; inside, tonight's date appears beside Isandro's true name—a name no living person knows. She hides the book, but the guildmaster's shadow lingers too long outside her door. Beat: dread blooming under routine.

chapters.title: The Guildmaster's Kindness
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Guildmaster Veyra offers Isandro a promotion—and a subtle test, asking about the prophecy book. Isandro lies for the first time in her career and feels the oath in her blood shift. Beat: the sick vertigo of deceiving family.

chapters.title: What the Fire Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Sefu. A fugitive dragon-warden smuggles himself into the city's underlevels, following the scent of stolen flame. He finds a guild warehouse of bottled dragon-fire and weeps at the theft. Beat: grief sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: An Unlikely Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Sefu confronts Isandro over a ledger entry; instead of fighting, they strike a wary deal—he'll show her what the fire truly is if she reads him the prophecy. Beat: two liars recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Broken Covenant
chapters.summary: POV Sefu. In an abandoned oath-hall, Sefu reveals the history: five swordspeakers once bound realms together; four were murdered by the guild's founders, their oath-stones scattered and sold. Beat: righteous fury and the weight of inherited guilt.

chapters.title: Hunted by Your Own
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Veyra declares Isandro a thief; guild enforcers hunt her through the rain-slicked city. She escapes only by using her swordspeech publicly for the first time in years. Beat: terror transforming into resolve.

chapters.title: The Thief Who Kept Books
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Hiding in a canal-side flophouse, Isandro meets Nour, a pickpocket who's been fencing guild goods unknowingly, and Tam, a disgraced guild clerk. Three outlaws around one candle. Beat: the first fragile warmth of found family.

chapters.title: First Oath-Stone
chapters.summary: POV Tam. The clerk leads them to a pawnshop where his old lover hoards a stone that hums when Isandro nears. Retrieving it costs a betrayal Tam must confess. Beat: shame met with unexpected forgiveness.

chapters.title: The Dragon Beneath the Harbor
chapters.summary: POV Sefu. Sefu brings the group to the last dragon, Ashveth, guttering beneath the harbor in a shell of salt and rust. She speaks to Isandro in dreams of debts unpaid. Beat: awe and terrible responsibility.

chapters.title: Veyra's Version
chapters.summary: POV Veyra. The guildmaster's chapter: she believes the covenant was tyranny and the thefts liberation, and she genuinely loves Isandro like a daughter. Beat: antagonist humanized; certainty made sympathetic.

chapters.title: The Price on the Door
chapters.summary: POV Nour. To buy passage to the mountain vaults, Nour sells her most precious stolen memory—the face of the mother she can't recall. Beat: survival's cost made intimate and irreversible.

chapters.title: Second Stone, Old Wound
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. The second oath-stone sits in Veyra's private vault. Isandro infiltrates her old home and finds letters proving Veyra knew about the prophecy all along. Beat: heartbreak braided with betrayal.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Salt Gate
chapters.summary: POV Tam. Enforcers ambush the group at the city gate; Tam takes a crossbow bolt shielding Nour. They escape by river barge, Tam feverish. Beat: love declared in crisis, fear of loss.

chapters.title: Third Stone, Drowned Choir
chapters.summary: POV Sefu. The third stone rests in a sunken temple guarded by drowned spirits who demand a song of true regret. Sefu sings of the wardens' failure to protect the dragons. Beat: penance and release.

chapters.title: The Prophecy's Fine Print
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Reading the prophecy fully, Isandro discovers the reforging requires a swordspeaker's life-flame—or the willing flame of four companions sharing the burden. She resolves to hide this from the others. Beat: the protector's lonely lie.

chapters.title: Ashveth's Last Bright Day
chapters.summary: POV Ashveth (dragon). The dying dragon recalls the first covenant's forging and judges each companion's heart in turn. She tells Isandro plainly: a lie kept from family will crack any covenant. Beat: mythic gravity, gentle rebuke.

chapters.title: Fourth Stone, Paid in Full
chapters.summary: POV Nour. The final stone is held by Veyra's enforcer-captain, whom Nour defeats not by force but by returning his own pawned memory of his daughter. Beat: mercy as strength; the theme crystallized.

chapters.title: The Emberhold
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. At the ruined forge-fortress, the group begins the reforging ritual as Veyra arrives with the guild's army. Isandro confesses her hidden sacrifice; her family refuses to let her die alone. Beat: truth breaking open before battle.

chapters.title: Covenant Reforged
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Climax: amid battle, four companions each give a portion of their flame while Isandro speaks the new oath—not obedience, but mutual care between realms. Ashveth blazes back to life; the stones fuse; Veyra, seeing the fire answer freely given love, lowers her blade. Beat: triumphant, costly, earned.

chapters.title: Ledgers Burned
chapters.summary: POV Veyra. Aftermath: the guild dissolves; stolen wonders are returned to their sources. Veyra, stripped of office but not exiled, chooses to help catalogue what must be given back. Beat: justice without vengeance; reconciliation attempted honestly.

chapters.title: The Wild Ember
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Seasons later, the found family keeps a small waystation where dragons and humans trade fairly—no ledgers, only promises witnessed aloud. Isandro writes one final line in a blank book: 'This story belongs to everyone who stayed.' Beat: warm, open-ended peace.
